description: The scoring and payout mechanism of the 600M retroactive distribution, stated in one place. NOTHING IS POSTED AND NOTHING IS ANCHORED: usage is counted on chain as it happens by UsageCounter, and RpgfMinter pays from those already-final numbers, so there is no root to post, no bond, no challenge and no formulaHash. The reward is UNIFORM (no tag, category or weight) and UNCAPPED; Sybil resistance is the two-sided LIVE ETH STAKE, not a formula lever. This file is the normative PROSE statement of what the contracts compute, and the machine-readable `parameters` the off-chain mirror (sdk/src/rpgf) derives its constants from. The mirror exists for display and verification — recomputing what the chain already holds — never for posting an answer. Integer arithmetic throughout; no floating point anywhere.

parameterUnits.scoreScale: 10^18, the fixed-point scale inside the cube root so flooring error is negligible
parameterUnits.trancheCount: RpgfMinter.TRANCHE_COUNT. Tranche i pays for UsageCounter period i; the two schedules are configured consistently at deploy.

recording.call: UsageCounter.recordUsage(order, artifact, sectionHash, proof) — permissionless. Only the section FINGERPRINT (keccak256 of the committed bytes) reaches calldata, never the preimage. The proof is what is trusted, never the caller; recording is gas-paid by whoever benefits, usually the artifact's author.
recording.resolvedOrder: The order hash is recomputed from the signed Commitment struct and FigaroCore.orderStatus(orderHash) must equal 2 (RESOLVED). Usage is what a settled process leaves behind: an open process counts for nothing, and an unknown order reverts.
recording.sellerStake: SELLER-SIDE LIVE-STAKE GATE: the process's seller-of-record (order.seller) must hold a live MembersRegistry stake — MembersRegistry.registered(order.seller) must be true. An unregistered or withdrawn seller's settled trade does NOT count (SellerNotStaked). Scope this honestly: it prices the SELLER IDENTITY, not breadth. d counts (buyer, seller) pairs and the buyer side is ungated by design, so a pair can still be fabricated for gas. Sybil resistance can only come from the cost of an identity — no scoring shape can separate a fabricated pair from a genuine one — so it is the registries' stake terms that carry it, never the formula.
recording.inclusion: The artifact must be merkle-included in the order's signed agreementHash under AttestationCoordinator's leaf shape, byte for byte: keccak256(bytes.concat(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(artifact, sectionHash)))). The artifact key is the ClauseRegistry idHash for a clause — keccak256(abi.encode(clauseId, version)) — or the AssemblyRegistry compositionHash for an assembly. There is no attestation, no provenance clause and no article classification in the counting path.
recording.period: Usage lands in UsageCounter.currentPeriod() — the first period whose end is still in the future. Once the last period has ended, accrual is closed forever and recordUsage reverts.
recording.idempotence: One process counts ONCE EVER per artifact — globally, not per period — in whichever period it is first recorded; a repeat reverts (AlreadyCounted). A resolved order stays resolved and its struct is public, so a per-period key would let the same trade be re-recorded in every period: that pays for recording gas rather than adoption, and lets one fabricated period-0 farm be milked across all three tranches. Each period therefore counts only the usage that is NEW to it, which is what the declining 300M/200M/100M schedule assumes.

accrual.c: Distinct settled processes that used the artifact in the period.
accrual.d: Distinct (buyer, seller) pairs across those processes in the period — incremented only on a pair's first counted process. A per-pair cap of 5 processes was deleted 2026-07-30: it never bound for an attacker optimising score per unit cost (whose optimum is one trade per fabricated pair, well under the cap), while it did bind honest repeat trade. The c^(1/3) exponent already discounts repetition far more steeply — a million trades between one pair score the same as a hundred distinct pairs trading once, at ten thousand times the cost.
accrual.score: score = icbrt(c * d * d * 10^18), where icbrt is the floor integer cube root — i.e. c^(1/3) * d^(2/3). UNIFORM across artifacts: no tag, category or weight multiplier, so every artifact's score is its real usage alone. Read it as score = d * (c/d)^alpha with alpha = 1/3: distinct relationships, times average repeat depth raised to alpha. Alpha is therefore the ELASTICITY OF REWARD TO REPEAT DEPTH (8x the depth earns 2x the score), and when every pair trades once (c = d) the score is the count itself for any alpha. alpha < 1/2 is justified because a new relationship informs more than another observation of a known one; alpha = 1/3 exactly is a JUDGMENT, not a derivation, and it is uniform across artifacts so it is not curation. It is NOT a Sybil defense and is not offered as one — no scoring shape can separate a fabricated pair from a genuine one, so resistance lives in the cost of an identity. Value is deliberately not a term: the protocol's cost to move one unit equals its cost to move a trillion.
accrual.totalScoreIn: The period's summed artifact scores, maintained in O(1) as a delta on every record. Final once the period ends.

payout.gate: RpgfMinter.claim(trancheId, artifacts) requires UsageCounter.periodClosed(trancheId): a tranche pays for its own period, whose counts stop moving the moment it ends. No snapshot, no checkpoint array, no history walk — and claims never expire, because a closed period's arithmetic is stable forever.
payout.authorOfRecord: Every passed artifact is verified against its own registry with a LIVE stake — ClauseRegistry.depositOf(idHash) must have registrar == caller AND withdrawn == false; AssemblyRegistry.bindings(compositionHash) must have author == caller AND depositWithdrawn == false. This is the AUTHOR-SIDE half of the live-ETH-stake gate: you earn RPGF only while your artifact's stake stays live. An artifact the caller does not author, or whose stake is withdrawn, reverts (NotAuthorOfRecord). The caller's list is a lookup key, never a claim of ownership.
payout.entitlement: score = sum of the caller's artifacts' scores for the period; amount = floor(trancheAmount[trancheId] * score / totalScoreIn(trancheId)). THE ARTIFACT LIST MUST BE DUPLICATE-FREE — a repeat reverts (DuplicateArtifact). Until 2026-07-30 duplicates were summed and the total then CLAMPED to the period total, so any author of a non-zero-scoring artifact could repeat it until the sum reached the denominator and mint the ENTIRE tranche; the clamp is what made it maximal, silently rounding a malformed claim up to the whole pool. With distinct artifacts score <= total holds structurally, so there is nothing to clamp. UNIFORM PRO RATA — no per-wallet cap. The reward tracks real usage directly, and the fixed pool is one a farmer dilutes, never inflates. Flooring dust stays unminted: the tranche amount is a ceiling, not a target.
payout.onceOnly: One claim per wallet per tranche — a wallet passes every artifact it authored in that single call. The budget is enforced twice: RpgfMinter.minted[trancheId] against trancheAmount, and the outer FlorinToken minter cap registered at genesis.

reads.description: Everything the mirror needs is public chain state. Log order is (blockNumber, logIndex) ascending.
consumed: UsageCounter.UsageRecorded(bytes32 indexed artifact, uint8 indexed period, bytes32 indexed processId, bytes32 pairKey, uint64 c, uint64 d, uint256 score)

MembersRegistry.MemberRegistered / MemberWithdrawalRequested — the seller-of-record's live-stake state (the seller-side gate). De-surfacing is the REQUEST, not the later ETH release: eligibility ends when the member asks to leave, while the deposit stays locked for the withdrawal cooldown.
ClauseRegistry.ClauseRegistered — the artifact's registrar of record (author-side gate reads depositOf.withdrawn)
AssemblyRegistry.AssemblyRegistered — the compositionHash's author of record
